To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The 68Ge level scheme has been extended to spin 7−.

(i) the level structure of the nuclei 68Ge and 74Kr has been established for the first time, (ii) the spin-parity of several levels in the nuclei 66Ge, 70Se and 82Sr has been determined for the first time and (iii) the spin-parities of several excited states of 68Ge, 69As and 80Sr have been confirmed by the angular distribution measurements.
the neutron deficient nuclei 66Ge and 68Ge have been populated in heavy-ion reactions for the first time and their excited states have been studied in-beam.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of nuclear structure properties in the region 32 < Z < 34, 28 < N < 30 and 34 < Z < 36, 30 < N < 34.
the investigation of neutron-deficient nuclei around the N = Z line in the mass range 60 ≤A ≤ 90.
the study of the structure of neutron deficient nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the level structure of neutron deficient nuclei with Z=30,32,34,36,38,40 is well established up to A=80.
the level schemes of the even-even nuclei66Ge,68,70,74,78Ge,80Sr,82Sr are now well established.
the level schemes of the neutron-deficient nuclei in the region of 28 have been completed and the spin and parity assignments of the levels are now well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experimental results are in agreement with the predictions of the shell model.
in the neutron deficient nuclei the ground state spin-parity assignment is often not the same as for the stable isobars.
the level schemes for 66Ge, 68Ge,69,70Se and74,80,82Sr have been completed, and that the level schemes of69As, 74Kr and 80Sr have been extended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 68Ge nucleus has a 2+ level at 1777.7 keV, a 3− level at 2649.0 keV, a (4+) level at 2267.8 keV and (6+) level at 3696.3 keV.
the neutron deficient nuclei in this region have a strong tendency to develop collectivity.
the 2+ states of66,68Ge and 70Se are at higher excitation energy than predicted by shell model calculations, which is a consequence of the large deformation of the 68Ni core.
